citation.title: Attention-based Deep Multiple Instance Learning
citation.authors: Maximilian Ilse; Jakub M. Tomczak; Max Welling
citation.venue: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR)

topic: Permutation-invariant attention pooling for bag-level classification in multiple instance learning
own_question: Can a trainable, attention-weighted MIL pooling match or improve bag classification and indicate key instances?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper models the bag label as Bernoulli. Its neural pipeline embeds instances, pools them with softmax attention (with a gated variant), and classifies the pooled representation. It reports results on classical MIL benchmarks, MNIST-bags, and two histopathology image datasets using cross-validation. It also shows attention heatmaps as a proxy for key instances. The task is static binary classification, with no time series, causal constraint, or plasma data.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant; instances within a bag are unordered and treated as independent, and there is no temporal target.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite it as evidence that attention aids causal nowcasting or CES/BES/ECEI fusion.
Do not treat attention weights as physical mechanism identification; the authors present them only as a proxy for key instances.
Do not imply our study uses MIL or attention pooling unless that was actually implemented.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: The paper's bag classification of unordered instances does not match our causal temporal regression of the current CES report. Cite it only if the paper discusses attention-based interpretability or set pooling as background, without any performance claims transferred from it.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
